metadata.title: Missing You: an unrushed place for who matters
metadata.description: The people and moments that matter deserve an unrushed place. Write about who you want to remember, what still stays with you, or what you are not ready to say yet. Your full text stays off-chain; only a proof is anchored on-chain. Others can verify a match without reading your words. Whether and when to share stays entirely up to you.

footer.tagline: Missing You: preserving memories with care.

qa.metaDescription: Simple answers about Missing You, privacy, and optional blockchain proof.
qa.title: Questions & answers
qa.intro: Short answers for everyday readers. If you want to go deeper, use the trusted links at the bottom; they open in a new tab.

faq.q: Do I need a wallet or crypto to write a memory?
faq.a: No. You can sign in with email and write like a normal website. A wallet is only needed if you choose to anchor proof on-chain.

faq.q: Is my full diary text stored on the blockchain?
faq.a: No. Your story stays in the app’s database (off-chain). The chain only receives a small fingerprint (a hash) and related metadata, not your full letter.
It means recording a tamper-evident fingerprint of your memory on a public ledger. Later, anyone can check that the same memory still matches that record, without reading your private text.
It’s optional. Some people want an independent, time-stamped record that isn’t controlled by one company. It’s about trust and verification, not trading coins.

faq.q: Will I make money from this?
faq.a: Missing You is not an investment product. Test networks may use test ETH with no real-world value. Always be careful with real money and scams elsewhere.

faq.q: What is a test network (e.g. Sepolia)?
faq.a: A practice network developers use so real money isn’t at risk. Think of it as a sandbox. The app may be configured to use one while you try things out.

blockchain.metaDescription: A simple explanation of blockchain and why Missing You uses it optionally.
blockchain.title: What is blockchain? Why use it here?
blockchain.lead: You don’t need to be technical. Here’s the idea in plain language.
blockchain.s1Body: A blockchain is a shared digital ledger many computers keep in sync. Once something is written according to the rules, it’s very hard to change it quietly, which helps with trust and timestamps.
blockchain.s2Body: Your words stay private in the app. If you want, you can anchor a fingerprint of your memory on-chain. That gives you an independent place to prove “this memory existed in this form at this time”, without publishing your full story.
blockchain.s3Body: We’re not selling tokens or promising returns. Wallet actions are for signing and optional anchoring. If someone asks you to “invest” in a memory app, be skeptical. That’s not what this is for.

howItWorks.metaDescription: A simple overview of how you write, save, optionally anchor, and share memories.
howItWorks.title: How this app works
howItWorks.lead: A calm flow: write first, prove only if you want, share only if you want.

steps.title: Sign in and write
steps.body: Create an account with email. Add a title, your memory, and optionally who it’s for. Everything feels like a normal journal app.

steps.title: Saved in the app
steps.body: Your text is stored securely in the app’s database. You can keep it private or mark it as shareable for a public page later.

steps.title: Optional: anchor a fingerprint
steps.body: If you connect a wallet, you can record a cryptographic fingerprint on a blockchain. That’s separate from your private text. It’s for verification, not for reading your diary on-chain.

steps.title: Optional: share
steps.body: When a memory is shareable, you can copy a public link so others read what you chose to share and see proof details if you anchored.

walletGuide.metaTitle: Connect a wallet & anchor a memory · Missing You
walletGuide.metaDescription: A beginner guide: when you need a wallet, how to connect MetaMask or other wallets, and how to anchor proof without blockchain background.
walletGuide.title: Connect a wallet and anchor a memory (beginner guide)
walletGuide.lead: You can write memories with email only. This page is for the moment you decide to put a cryptographic proof on-chain. No prior crypto knowledge required.
walletGuide.s1Title: Do I need to install MetaMask?
walletGuide.s1Body: Not unless you want to anchor. Writing and saving drafts works like a normal website after you sign in with email. When you are ready to anchor, you need a wallet that can sign transactions on the network this app uses. MetaMask is a common choice (browser extension and mobile app), but it is not the only one. The app also supports WalletConnect, which lets many mobile wallets connect by scanning a QR code. If you already use another Ethereum-compatible wallet in your browser, it may appear as “injected” when you click connect.
walletGuide.s2Title: What is a wallet, in everyday words?
walletGuide.s2Body: Think of it as a keychain for your blockchain identity. It stores cryptographic keys, shows you transaction requests in plain language as best it can, and asks you to approve or reject. It does not replace your Missing You account: email login still controls your memories in the app. The wallet is mainly for signing the anchor transaction and paying network fees when you choose to anchor.
walletGuide.s3Title: How to connect your wallet here
walletGuide.s3Body: Open the site menu (top right), then choose “Connect wallet”. Pick MetaMask, WalletConnect, or another option your browser offers. Approve the connection in your wallet popup. If nothing happens, check that the extension is unlocked or try refreshing once. On mobile, WalletConnect is often the smoothest path.
walletGuide.s4Title: Networks, fees, and test vs real money
walletGuide.s4Body: Anchoring always targets one specific blockchain network that the app is configured for (for example Ethereum mainnet or a test network). Your wallet must be on that same network when you sign. Publishing a transaction costs a small network fee paid in the chain’s native coin (for example ETH on Ethereum), not paid to Missing You. On test networks, faucets give away free test coins so you can practice. On mainnet, you need real coins you bought or transferred yourself, and prices move with network traffic.
walletGuide.s5Title: How to anchor a memory, step by step
anchorSteps: Write or open a draft memory and make sure you are happy with the text. Anchoring is optional and happens only when you choose it.
Connect your wallet from the menu and switch to the network the app expects (your wallet will usually prompt you, or the app will ask you to switch).
Open the memory you want to anchor and find the “Anchor to blockchain” section.
Read the short explanation: only a memory key and content hash go on-chain, not your full journal text.
Click the anchor button and confirm the transaction in your wallet. Wait until the network confirms.
If the app shows a success state, your proof is stored. You can copy the transaction hash to view it on a public block explorer.
walletGuide.s6Body: Transactions can fail when the network is busy, the fee is too low, or you reject the request in the wallet. You can try again with a fresh fee suggestion. If the chain succeeded but the app looks stuck, some screens let you paste the confirmed transaction hash to sync state. When in doubt, check your wallet’s activity tab for the latest status.
walletGuide.s7Body: Never share your wallet seed phrase or password with anyone, including support. Bookmark the real site URL. Missing You will never ask you to “invest” or send tokens to unlock anchoring. If a popup or site asks for your seed phrase, close it.
walletGuide.helpIconTooltip: Open the beginner guide: wallets and anchoring (new tab).

privacySecurity.metaDescription: How Missing You handles your memories, optional blockchain proof, rate limits, and operational security.
privacySecurity.title: Privacy & security
privacySecurity.lead: This page summarizes how we approach safety and trust for a grief-sensitive product. It is not legal advice; it complements the technical documentation for operators.

sections.title: Where your words live
sections.body: Full journal text is stored in the application database (off-chain), not on a public blockchain. Only optional fingerprints (hashes) and related metadata are written on-chain when you choose to anchor. Private entries are not exposed to other visitors through the app’s public routes.

sections.title: Optional anchoring & wallets
sections.body: Connecting a wallet is only required for anchoring or for certain shareability changes on anchored memories. Network fees are paid to the blockchain, not to Missing You. Your email account and your on-chain transaction sender can differ; the proof record follows the wallet that submitted the anchor transaction.

sections.title: Abuse protection (API rate limits)
sections.body: Authenticated API routes apply per-user rate limits (for example creating memories, preparing or confirming anchors, and wallet-link challenges). When a limit is exceeded, the API responds with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After hint. Limits are enforced in-process on each server instance; for multi-instance production, consider a shared limiter (for example Redis) so thresholds stay global.

sections.title: Monitoring
sections.body: Operators should ship structured logs, alerts, and runbooks for production. The codebase emits JSON logs including rate-limit events; wire your preferred observability stack (for example Sentry, Datadog, or cloud-native tools) per your deployment guide.

sections.title: What you can do
sections.body: Use a strong, unique password on your email provider, keep your wallet seed phrase private, and review shareability before copying a public link. If something looks wrong with verification, compare the proof panel on the public page with the block explorer entry.

home.headline: Preserve a memory with proof that it existed.
home.subhead: A calm place for memories that matter. Keep your words private off-chain, and anchor only the proof on-chain so anyone can verify integrity without reading your journal.

blockchainStory.title: This product can write to a blockchain. Here is the honest version
blockchainStory.intro: No jargon quiz required. As you scroll, three beats: what we put on-chain, what a blockchain is, and why that might matter for a memory.
blockchainStory.usesTitle: What Missing You actually does on-chain
blockchainStory.usesBody: Your journal text stays off-chain in the app. If you choose to anchor, we publish a cryptographic fingerprint and related metadata to a public network so the entry can be verified later, without pasting your full story on-chain.
blockchainStory.whatBody: Picture a shared ledger many independent computers keep in sync. Once information is written under the rules, revising history quietly becomes extremely difficult, which is why people reach for it when they care about order, integrity, and a public audit trail.
blockchainStory.whyBody: It is optional. Some people want proof that does not rest on a single company’s database: a way to show “this commitment existed in this form” that anyone can check. The point is verifiability, not trading tokens.

writeTrust.toggleLabel: Where your words go (privacy & optional proof)
writeTrust.lead: A one-minute overview before you write:
bullets: Your full memory text is saved in Missing You’s database — not on a public blockchain.
“Private” means other visitors cannot open your entry through the app; we treat private pages as not found.
If you later choose to anchor, only a cryptographic fingerprint and metadata go on-chain — never your full letter.
You can use the product as a simple journal and ignore wallets entirely.
writeTrust.footer: Questions? Open Privacy & security or Q & A from the footer.

onboarding.welcomeBody: This is a quiet place to write about someone you miss. There is no feed, no likes — just your words, saved carefully.
onboarding.trustTitle: Privacy and proof, in plain words
onboarding.trustLead: A few things worth knowing up front:
trustBullets: Your journal text stays off-chain in our systems unless you choose a shareable page.
Blockchain here is optional: it can record a tamper-evident fingerprint of a memory, not your full story.
You can skip wallets and anchoring entirely and still use Missing You as a private journal.
onboarding.ctaBody: Start with one short memory — a detail, a voice, a small moment. You can always come back to write more.

blockchain.title: Anchor to blockchain
blockchain.body: Only a bytes32 memory key and your content hash are sent on-chain, never your journal text.
anchorSteps: The server prepares a stable fingerprint (hash) of your memory — your prose is not uploaded in the transaction.
Your wallet must be on the same network the app uses for anchoring (check the site menu or settings).
You approve one transaction; a small network fee goes to the chain, not to Missing You.
After confirmation, this page updates so readers can match your text to the on-chain record.

proofClarity.title: What “verification” means here
proofClarity.verifiedIntro: When a memory is anchored, a reader can check:
verifiedBullets: A fingerprint (hash) of the memory was committed on a public network at a given time.
The text you see still matches that fingerprint, using the app’s published rules.
Basic metadata (for example shareability) lines up with what the registry stores.
limitsBullets: That the story is factually “true” in a legal sense — only that it matches a recorded commitment.
That the site will always stay online; availability still depends on the operator and hosting.
That every word was written by a particular legal identity — only that the chosen wallet paid for the anchor transaction.
